A1.justification: Both are complete, readable 34-page versions of GriDiT, including Appendices A and B. Pages 2–34 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; page 1 differs only in the code-availability sentence and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: V1 reports original video and CT-volume generation experiments in Section 4, plus appendix denoising, super-resolution, and additional baseline results.

after.justification: V2 retains the same original empirical results, including Tables 1–8 and the qualitative comparisons in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The two-stage grid-based DiT method, 3D positional embeddings, super-resolution module, and autoregressive sampling procedure are unchanged in Section 3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use SkyTimelapse, Taichi, Minecraft, and CT-RATE, retaining the same sequence-generation, CT-denoising, and super-resolution tasks and scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, including Diffusion Forcing on Minecraft, GenerateCT on CT-RATE, SinSR for super-resolution, and the naive baselines in Table 8.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.7 retain the same splits, resolutions, training settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures, including cyclic looping of test videos for longer-sequence evaluation.

E4.justification: The grid-size and positional-embedding ablations, attention visualizations, super-resolution comparisons, naive-representation analyses, and qualitative sampling studies are identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported performance results.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged, including Tables 1–8 and Appendix B. For example, Table 1 retains full-data GriDiT results of FVD 998.43, FID 54.8, and sampling time 53.8 seconds.

T1.justification: The probabilistic factorization, diffusion equations, formal grid and sampling descriptions, and positional-embedding definitions are unchanged, including Equations 1–5 and Appendices A.2–A.6.

C1.justification: The claims about synthesis quality, arbitrary-length generation, efficiency, and applicability across domains remain unchanged. The abstract edit concerns code access.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including fine-motion loss, interpolation smoothing, computational constraints, and the unestablished medical utility of synthetic CT volumes in Section 5 and Appendix A.11.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces 'We will make our implementation publicly available' with 'Code is available at our project page' and adds a project-page hyperlink. This updates code-access information; implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and Listing 1 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A.1, and the references are identical. No cited research, novelty positioning, or comparison-scope rationale changes.

P1.justification: One sentence at the end of the abstract is revised, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. All other prose, terminology, section organization, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–18, Tables 1–8, captions, placements, and page layout are unchanged. The revised abstract sentence and version stamp do not reorganize the first page.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a project-page hyperlink for code where v1 offered a future-release promise, modestly improving access information for reproducibility. Scientific content and evidence, including the appendices, are unchanged. The linked code's actual availability and usability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.
